segmentName: Woven, Knitted & Non-Woven Interlinings (garment construction support fabric)

market.worldSizeUSD_B_range: Global garment interlining market: $3.65B (2025) to $4.67B by 2030 (5.0-5.3%/yr).
exportGeographies: not confirmed current for companies in this segment — general note: interlining demand is tied to India's own garment-export corridors (US/EU/UAE buyers of Indian-made apparel) since interlining is typically an internal input, not a directly-exported finished good
market.domesticSlice: India's 'shirts' sub-segment of the interlining market is estimated at ~$0.90B, ~20% share of the global category, growing ~6.8%/yr — driven by India's shirt-manufacturing/export base and cost-effective TPV interlining adoption. Asia-Pacific is the largest and fastest-growing region for interlinings generally, led by China, India and Bangladesh's garment-manufacturing base.

structureFacts: India's garment-export corridors (principally serving US/EU/UAE apparel buyers) are the primary structural demand driver, since interlining is an internal construction input, not a standalone export product

adoptionStructure.note: Recurring bulk/contract orders tied to seasonal fashion-buying cycles and the underlying apparel-export order book — not an independent repurchase-rate category

peers.name: Bindal Cotex Pvt. Ltd.
peers.note: India fusible-interlining maker since 1991/1993, Delhi; 21 employees (FY ending Mar 2024); ISO 9001:2000 (DNV Norway) certified; capacity 500,000+ m/month

drivers: technical consultancy/testing support bundled with product
price-performance positioning versus European incumbents (Freudenberg et al.) for mid-to-high-end Indian garment exporters

steps: offer woven, knitted, and non-woven interlining fabrics (fusible and sew-in)
differentiate by GSM, stretch behavior, and certifications (Oeko-Tex/GRS)
develop application-specific formulations (collar/cuff, blazer canvas, stretch fabrics)
hold certification compliance (Oeko-Tex, GRS, buying-house approvals)
maintain ready-stock inventory and multi-city warehousing to meet fast-fashion lead times
provide technical consultancy/testing support bundled with product
compete on price-performance vs. European incumbents
receive recurring bulk/contract orders from garment manufacturers and export houses
reorder tied to underlying apparel-export order books
